## Before PR #108

Before PR #108, the worker sent the entire pending queue in a single batch. The fixture shows this behavior across three files.

In `config.ts`, the configuration exported only the endpoint, `'/jobs'`. There was no batch-limit setting or validation for such a setting in the shown code.

In `queue.ts`, `drain(pending)` returned `pending.splice(0)`. This removed every item from the supplied array and returned those items as the drained batch. The function accepted no limit, so callers could not request a bounded number of jobs.

In `worker.ts`, `tick(pending, send)` imported the endpoint and the drain function, then called `await send(endpoint, drain(pending))`. Each tick therefore removed all pending jobs and passed them to one send call. The batch size depended on the number of jobs waiting when the drain occurred.

## Gap and motivation

The PR body identifies the gap directly: each send received the entire pending queue. The intended change is to cap the number of jobs passed to each send while leaving the rest queued for later drains.

The diff introduces `BATCH_LIMIT`, defaults it to `100`, and rejects values that are not positive integers during configuration initialization. It also adds a `limit` parameter to `drain`, uses `pending.splice(0, limit)`, and passes the configured limit from the worker. These changes connect the configuration value to the queue operation that determines batch size.

The stated scope is specifically a bound on job count per batch. The body explicitly says this does not bound job memory or processing time. It also excludes per-tenant scheduling because the queue currently has no tenant key. The fixture documents no alternatives or follow-up issues.
